claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles are boiled in shared water; the kitchen handles wheat noodles, miso/soy tare and flour-thickened broths throughout, so cross-contact with gluten is unavoidable.
Shoyu-tonkotsu bowls and the miso tare rely on standard Japanese soy/miso seasoning, which typically contains wheat; no wheat-free tare is indicated.
All broths are animal-based (pork bone, chicken, seafood/dried fish) and there is no separate plant-based stock, so no dish can be made vegan.
Broths are made entirely from scratch with no chemical seasonings or instant products, simmered and matured over one to two days, with a stated low-sodium, body-friendly aim.

name: らぁめん みや (Raamen Miya)

claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles are boiled in shared water and the soy-based tare typically contains wheat, served over a pork-bone broth — not safe for gluten avoidance.
The broth is finished with a soy (shoyu) tare in the Daiichi Asahi lineage; Japanese shoyu almost always contains wheat.
The broth is pork-bone (豚骨) based and bowls are topped with abundant pork chashu; no plant-based preparation exists.

name: らぁ～めん京 祇園本店 (Raamen Miyako Gion Honten)

claims.text: Bowls are built on house wheat thin noodles boiled in shared water, with soy/miso tare and chicken-vegetable broth; no gluten-free preparation is offered.
Soy (醤油) is one of the standard tare options; ordinary Japanese shoyu contains wheat, and no wheat-free tare is indicated.
The base broth is animal (chicken paitan) and bowls include pork chashu and egg; no vegan option is offered.
Wheat ramen noodles are boiled in shared water and the broth/tare is built on a wheat-containing soy base; no gluten-free preparation exists here.
Shoyu-forward Kyoto-style tare; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat and there is no indication of a wheat-free alternative.
Broth is chicken- and pork-bone based with back-fat; menu is meat- and egg-centric, so cross-contact with animal products is pervasive throughout the kitchen.

name: ラーメン 豚やどっ (Ramen Buta Yado)

claims.text: Bowls are built on house-made wheat noodles and a wheat-based Kyoto soy-sauce (Goko) tare; everything passes through the same shared noodle water and kitchen, so gluten is unavoidable and cross-contact is pervasive.
The tare is built on Goko, a traditional Kyoto soy sauce — a standard fermented soy sauce that contains wheat.
The broth is made exclusively from pork (arm meat and back fat) and the shop's whole identity is heaped pork chashu; there is no plant-based option and animal product is in every bowl.

name: ラーメン 大栄 本店 (Ramen Daiei Honten)

claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles are boiled in shared water in a single small counter kitchen; gluten cross-contamination is unavoidable.
Shoyu and miso ramen are the house specialties; the soy-sauce/miso tare is almost certainly wheat-based, as is standard for this style. No wheat-free tare is indicated.
Broth is pork-based and bowls are built around chashu pork; no vegan or vegetarian broth is offered, so all items share animal-based stock.

name: ラーメン大戦争 京都河原町店 (Ramen Daisenso Kyoto Kawaramachi)

claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles are boiled in shared water and the kitchen is built around wheat-based shoyu tare; gluten cross-contact is unavoidable.
Signature bowls are Kansai-dashi shoyu (soy-sauce) ramen; Japanese shoyu tare is brewed from wheat, so the seasoning base contains gluten.
Broths are made from chicken bone and scallop with fish/dashi elements, and chashu pork is central — no plant-based option and pervasive animal-product use.

name: ラーメン藤 京都本店 (Ramen Fuji Kyoto Honten)

claims.text: A noodle-factory-direct shop built around wheat ramen noodles; flour is central to the operation and cross-contact with wheat is unavoidable.
The broth is a soy-based 豚骨醤油 tare; standard Japanese shoyu contains wheat, so the soup base should be assumed to contain wheat.
Broth and toppings are pork-based (pork-bone soy broth, pork rice, gyoza); no plant-based options noted.
